Our Mission
Every shipment
arrives as promised

AFA stands for Africa Fast Arrival. We take the steps that are normally split across a chain of suppliers — booking, export declaration, main leg, customs clearance, inland haulage and final delivery — and put them on one order, under one accountable party. No more chasing four vendors for one container.

The value of logistics is not the lowest number on a quotation. It is that the cargo actually arrives, arrives on time, and costs what you were told it would cost.

Business Segments

What we do

Built around the full China–East Africa trade lane: sea and air, door to door.

Sea Freight

FCL and LCL from major Chinese ports to Mombasa, including booking, haulage, export declaration and destination handling.

Air Freight

Time-critical and high-value cargo from China to Nairobi, with airport clearance and delivery.

Customs Clearance

A local clearance team handles declaration, inspection, duties and release — compliance first.

Inland Transport

Line-haul along the Mombasa–Nairobi corridor, with fleet capacity and milestone tracking.

Warehousing

Consolidation in China and transit storage at destination: stuffing, de-stuffing, short-term storage and distribution.

Last-mile Delivery

Door delivery in Nairobi and surrounding towns, with delivery milestones and traceable proof of receipt.

Cross-border

Onward movement from the Kenyan hub into neighbouring East African Community (EAC) markets.

Digital Platform

Orders, quotes, documents and live status online — supported by an AI-native operations and service team.

Full-Term Fulfillment

Every Incoterm
Sea and air

We take on FOB, CIF, DAP and DDP as the customer actually needs them, not just the easiest leg. Under DDP we arrange transport, clearance and duty payment ourselves, so what you get is a landed cost you can rely on.

Operations

Every node
in our own hands

Warehouse, yard, clearance desk and control room are stages of one process, not separate companies. We keep people and data at the nodes that matter, so exceptions surface when they happen — not when the customer asks.
